publication: Alex Kruckman, Model Theory Lecture Notes, updated 2018-12-14. Author-hosted 92-page PDF; printed page equals one-based PDF page. This is a different version from the Math 509 notes updated 2025-12-18.

reviews.checked_passages: Model-theory expansion: §5.1 pp.46–49, partial and complete types, Propositions 5.1 and 5.3; §6.1 pp.58–61, finite relational ages, Proposition 6.1 and the necessity of amalgamation in Theorem 6.6; §6.3 pp.74–76, model completeness and Theorem 6.25. Later type-omission/saturation and Fraïssé-construction passages were inspected for planning, not certified here as whole chapters.
reviews.outcome: KRUCKMAN-MT18-02 records the missing nonempty-class hypothesis in the age/Fraisse characterizations; the corpus states it explicitly. No other serious defect found in the adopted compactness and relative preservation arguments. Possibly empty finite structures, nullary relations and literal-copy transport are explicit. KRUCKMAN-MT18-01 records a local negation typo in Theorem6.25, corrected in the corpus. Algebraic examples and topological type-space arguments are outside this check.

reviews.checked_passages: §6.1 pp.59–62: Fraisse-limit definition, Proposition6.2, Lemma6.3, Corollaries6.4–6.5 and Theorem6.6, including the specified-map AP square and every finite extension task.
reviews.outcome: KRUCKMAN-MT18-02 supplies the missing nonempty-class hypothesis. KRUCKMAN-MT18-03 records a local wrong-object name in the construction; the commuting diagram has the correct target. The corpus replaces the online countable-row schedule by successive finite batches, with the original finite stage retained while enumerating each batch. No other serious defect found in the adopted construction/uniqueness arguments.

reviews.checked_passages: §6.3 pp.77–78, companion and model-companion definitions, Proposition6.28 and Exercise31; alternating embeddings and equality of universal consequences.
reviews.outcome: No new serious defect found in the adopted companion-theory arguments. The corpus spells out the two cofinal elementary subsequences of the alternating embedding chain, permits inconsistent theories, and distinguishes semantic equivalence from equality of axiom sets. General existentially closed-model constructions and algebraic examples are outside this entry.

reviews.checked_passages: §7.2 printed p.84, isolation definition and unavoidable realization; §7.3 printed p.90, Theorem7.17 finite/isolation implications. Actual PDF pages/footers inspected.
reviews.outcome: No new serious defect found in these adopted claims. The corpus proves the finite-type/isolation equivalence directly by formula separation and compactness, without topological prerequisites, and the argument also applies to satisfiable incomplete theories. Unavoidable realization separately assumes completeness of the theory. Lemma7.6 was inspected for later atomic-model planning; algebraic examples are not adopted. KRUCKMAN-MT18-04 records the missing q≠p restriction in the final separating conjunction; the corpus includes it and the empty-conjunction case.

reviews.checked_passages: Example6.10 printed pp.64–65, graph axioms, extension requests and the binary-digit construction.
reviews.outcome: No serious defect established in these adopted passages. The corpus states freshness explicitly for both finite prescribed sets, includes empty sides and repeated tuple coordinates in the m,n schema, and proves shared-syntax quantifier elimination through specified finite maps. Kruckman's weaker displayed schema also gives fresh witnesses by finite padding; its omitted explicit inequalities are not a false assertion. Probability and the zero-one law are outside this entry.

reviews.checked_passages: Theorem7.10 printed pp.85–88 and countable-family adaptation of Theorem7.12 p.88: finite avoidance, Henkin tasks and countable omission.
reviews.outcome: No new serious defect found beyond SCHLICHT-04, now repaired in the corpus. The adopted argument explicitly lifts finite constant support to free variables, includes repeated tuple names through equality constraints, keeps each added condition finite, and covers countably many varying finite arities. Omission is asserted for the named elementary submodel, not an arbitrary ambient model; the latter distinction is proved in the question. Broader topological or meager-set omission results are outside this entry.

reviews.checked_passages: Section7.1 printed pp.81–82, saturation definition, pushforward types and Theorem7.2 universality/uniqueness.
reviews.outcome: No serious defect found in the adopted countable arguments. SCHLICHT-05 records local source/target/index slips repaired by using the inverse of the current extended map and the correct model/parameter set. The corpus does not need language countability for these finite-parameter extension arguments, allows finite carriers, retains exact initial maps, and distinguishes omega-saturation from saturation of an arbitrary uncountable structure. No general-cardinal construction, algebraic or topological examples are adopted.

reviews.checked_passages: Section7.2 printed pp.84–86, Lemma7.6/Proposition7.7, Theorem7.9 and Corollary7.11; Theorem7.14 printed p.89, atomic/prime existence and isolating refinements.
reviews.outcome: No new serious defect found. KRUCKMAN-MT18-05 records a local wrong-model inference in the source atomic embedding proof. The corpus uses source atomicity and the exact supplied finite map. The density/existence equivalence is implemented by an explicit finite-stage named-tuple Henkin refinement construction, reusing the concrete support formula and avoiding topological or arbitrary-family omission premises. Field examples are outside this scope.

reviews.checked_passages: Theorem7.17 printed p.90 and Exercise39 printed p.91, finite type/formula/categoricity equivalences and uniform local finiteness.
reviews.outcome: No new serious defect found. The corpus uses omission and prescribed-map atomic uniqueness, without saturation or topology prerequisites. The finite isolation theorem already corrects KRUCKMAN-MT18-04. Shared-syntax formula classes and concrete type truth-set/profile injections establish the finite equivalences; finite parameter closures and the uniform term-generator bound are proved explicitly. Equality and dense-order examples reuse the corrected weak-order classifications, including repeated coordinates.

reviews.checked_passages: Theorem7.3 printed p.82 and Corollary7.13 printed p.88: smallness, finite-parameter type counting, countable saturated/universal models and atomic-model existence.
reviews.outcome: No new serious defect found in the adopted results. The corpus supplies the constant-to-free-variable truth/recovery argument, an inner countable request enumeration followed by an outer elementary chain, and explicit finite/empty cases. Prime-model existence uses the earlier countable varying-arity omission theorem directly, without topological prerequisites. Existence of an elementary-universal model is distinguished from saturation of a particular universal model.

reviews.checked_passages: Example7.18 printed pp.91–92 and Theorem7.19 printed p.92, the three named dense-order models and Vaught's never-two argument.
reviews.outcome: No new serious defect found in the adopted results. The corpus gives explicit rational ordered sums instead of sequences converging to real limits, proves the interval/tail classification and named-language completeness from the existing original-language quantifier elimination, and derives smallness from a finite representative family. The third-model argument distinguishes the original parameter indices from their new interpretations and uses the arbitrary finite-constant saturation bridge. Later spectrum bounds and Vaught-conjecture material are not adopted.

reviews.checked_passages: Example7.16 printed p.89: the order naming every rational, isolated point types, cut types, prime-model existence and failure of smallness.
reviews.consumers: [Named tuple isolators](entries/named-rational-order/entry.html#tuple-isolators); [specified unique prime embedding](entries/named-rational-order/entry.html#rational-prime); [continuum many types](entries/named-rational-order/entry.html#continuum-types); [no countable saturated model](entries/named-rational-order/entry.html#no-countable-saturation).
reviews.outcome: No new serious defect found in these adopted results. The corpus proves atomicity by explicit coordinate equalities and retains the specified rational inclusion in the named real model. Real-point types supply an injection, rather than an asserted exhaustive classification; an above-all-names type is explicitly outside their image. The upper bound uses countable syntax and applies to arbitrary theories in finite contexts. Naming infinitely many points is distinguished from finite parameter expansions, with no topological prerequisites.

reviews.checked_passages: Example7.15 printed p.89: the countably infinite unary coordinate language, quantifier elimination, complete one-type classification and failure of atomic/countable saturated model existence.
reviews.outcome: No new serious defect found in the adopted claims. The corpus supplies both the actual finite-subset and power-set models, handles all literal-conjunction equality/contradiction cases, and proves the specified complete-type bijection. Finite formula support and a changed predicate coordinate establish nonisolation. Prime and countable saturated/elementary-universal nonexistence use earlier existence criteria. Topological omission and the countable-model spectrum are outside this entry.

reviews.checked_passages: Printed pp.6–7 and33–34: function-closed carriers, substructures, generated carriers and ordinary embeddings; one-sorted specialization with the corpus nonempty-model convention. Also planning inspection of printed pp.50–57 and78–79 for the authorized union/existential-closure branch; those new consumers will be assessed at integration.
reviews.outcome: No serious defect found in the adopted foundation passages. The source permits empty carriers in its general sorted setting; the corpus distinguishes possibly empty function-closed carrier data from its nonempty structures and models. Ground terms, absent constants, repeated parameter coordinates and specified embedding images are explicit. Later source results are planning inspection only until their new entries are integrated.

reviews.checked_passages: Printed pp.50–52 supporting diagram and separation methods; §5.4 pp.53–56, directed unions, Proposition5.14 and Theorem5.15.
reviews.outcome: No serious defect found in the adopted union arguments. The corpus gives a direct theory-specific universal-diagram and exact-map elementary-factorization proof, then interleaves ordinary and elementary chains. Empty quantifier blocks, nullary symbols and inconsistent theories are explicit. KRUCKMAN-MT18-06 records the local repeated direction label in Theorem5.15.

reviews.checked_passages: Printed p.75, Proposition6.23; pp.78–79, Propositions6.30–6.31 and Theorem6.32: model completeness, existentially closed extensions and the model-companion criterion.
reviews.outcome: No new serious defect or local slip found in these adopted passages. The corpus supplies fixed-cardinal downward-Löwenheim–Skolem bounds and coded set-sized choices, tracks the original model map through recoding, and separates the inner request pass from the outer omega passes handling new parameters. The companion criterion derives original-theory model status rather than assuming axiom containment. Missing source bookkeeping is an exposition addition, not a confirmed error. Algebraic examples outside strict linear orders are not adopted.
